cells.location: Eastern wall of the Prakara
cells.remarks: This inscription records the gift of lands located in the village of Sadaiyan Kuricchi to the temple as "Thirumadaippallippuram." === TAMIL ORIGINAL === 30. On the westem wall of the Prakara of the temple - Later Pandya - -Sadaiyavarman Kulasekara Pandya -Records the gift of land by an individual of this village by name Murkulan Narayanan for a perpetual lamp. 31.Inscribed on a pilllar in the Southern corner of the prakara of the temple - Chola- Parantaka I (907- 953 A.D.,) - Records the gift of 31 sheep by one individual by name Kotran kilavan, who is said to have hailed from Kadanur, a village that was within Mallinadu, to the temple for a burning a perpetual lamp. 32. On the eastern wall of the first prakara of the temple - Later Pandya Sundhara Pandya - (1216-1239 A.D.,) - Records the gift of land by an individual by name Atthiraiyan Kundredutthan Srivallaban to meet out the expenses of the Ghee Abhishekam ( Neyyadal) to the deity during the Avani festival. 33. On the innerside of the western wall of the first prakara of the temple -Later Pandya - Kulasekara Pandya -Rcords the gift of fifty sheep by a lady by name Kotra Nacchiyar for a perpetual lamp to be burnt in the temple. The donar is mentioned as the wife of Asipatthanarayanan, a resident of Thirutthangal. 34. Inscribed on the western wall of the first prakara -Later Pandya - Kulasekara Pandya -Records the gift of 13 sheep by a lady by name Uyyavandhal, a native of Srivanavanmadevicchaturvedimangalam, which was located within venbu nadu, to the Perumal temple for the purpose of burning a ‘ Sandya Deepam’. 35. On the innerside of the north wail of the first prakara of the temple - Later Pandya- Kulasekara - Kulasekara Pandya - 13th century A.D., - Records the gift of 20 cows to the temple. 36. On the western portion of the northern wall of the first prakara -Later Pandya -Maravaran Sundharapandiyan -( 1216- 1239 A.D.,) - Records gift of land. 37. On the western wall of first prakara of the temple - Pandya- Records the Thirumadaippallipuram lands. It also mentions the actions taken to irrigate certain lands which were so far in uncultivated condition. New settlement also were made in that spe- cific area so that there will be enough population to take up the work of irrigation. 38. At the entrance popularly known as Paramapatha vasal of the temple - 13th century A.D., The donors name is recorded as Putridankondan alias Thirucchitrambalapperian, a native of Anandhur. 39. On the roof of the Sukkiravarakkuradu of the temple - 1885 A.D., -Records that Rengasamy Naicker, the Zamindar of Nagalapuram had donated this Mandapam (Sukkiravarakkuradu). 40. On the wall of the entrance of Sengamala Nacchiyar Shrine of the temple - Pandya- Jadavarman Srivallaban, (1090- 1116 A.D.,) - Damaged inscription. 41.On the northern side of the temple - 17th - 18th century A.D., -Hero stone in- scription - Records the ‘ratthakkani’ ( land donated to a person in praise of his blood Sac- rifice) gift given in praise of Ulli Bomman Kalangatha Kantanayakkar, a servant of Varadungarama Thanippuli Kantanayakkar. 185 === ENGLISH TRANSLATION === 30. cells.remarks: The 10 inscriptions found on the Gopura, mandapa, and pillars of the Vikkiramapandeesvaramudaiyar temple belong to the Later Pandya period. These record information regarding the construction of the Gopuram, the conducting of festivals, and the gifting of pillars and mandapas.
cells.tamil_fields: விக்ரமபாண்டீஸ்வரமுடையார் கோயிலின் கோபுரம், மண்டபம் மற்றும் தூண்களில் உள்ள 10 கல்வெட்டுகள், பிற்காலப் பாண்டியர் காலத்தைச் சேர்ந்தவை. இவை கோபுரம் கட்டியது, திருவிழா நடத்தியது, தூண்கள் மற்றும் மண்டபங்கள் தானமாக வழங்கப்பட்டது குறித்த செய்திகளைத் தெரிவிக்கின்றன.
cells.inscription_text:
CHOLAPURAM
1.On the Souther pillar of the Gopura of the Vikkiramapandeesvaramudaiyar temple
at cholapuram - Later Pandya - Sundhara Pandya - 13th century A.D., - Records that this
Gopuram was built in the name of the ruler Sundhara Pandian.
2. On the Southern pillar of the second Gopura of Vikkiramapandeesvara mudaiyar
- Later Pandya 13th century A.D., - Records that this Gopuram was built in the name of a
certain “Thambikku Nallar’.
3. On the northern pillar of the second Gopura of Vikkiramapandeesvaramudaiyar
temple - Later Pandya - 13th century A.D., - Records that the door jamp of the seond
Gopura of this temple was contributed by a certain Udaiyan udaiyan alias Sundarapandiyap
Pallavaraiyan, who belonged to the ‘Akapparivaran’.
4. On the Southern base of the second Gopura of the
Vikkiramapandeesvaramudaiyar temple - Later Pandya - Kulasekara Deva - Records a
certain festival with procession of the image of the god popularly known by the name
“Kulasekaran thiruadal thiruppavani”. This festival was conducted by the Sri Rudra Sri
Mahesvaras of the temple of Vikkirama Pandisvaramudaiyanayanar. The expenses of this
festival was met out from the rent realised on a house presented to the temple by a certain
Thennilangai Valanjiyar, Sorrakan Kadanthan Umaiyorupakan, residing in the street of
Narpatthennayiravan Peruntheru in Mudivalangupandya nallur located within Anmar Nadu.
5. On a pillar in the Natarajamandapa of Vikkramapandisvaramudaiyar at
Cholapuram -Later Pandya - 13th century - Records that this pillar was gifted by a certain
Sothi Sutriyan Sundharapperuman of Nangur.
6. On a pillar in the South eastern portion of the Natarajarmandapam of
Vikkiramapandisvaramudaiyar temple - Later Pandya - 13th century A.D., - Records that
this pillar was gifted by a certain Sadaiya Mandhirikal of Cholakulanthakapuram alias Kulatthu
Valuthiyur.
7. On the stone pillared mandapa located in front of the Natarajar mandapa of
Vikkiramapandisvaramudaiyar temple - Later Pandya - 13th century A.D., - Records that
this mandapa was contructed in the name of Periyan Perumal alias Venavudaiyar of
Pirambilur.
8. On the stone pillared mandapa seen in front of Nataraja Mandapa of Vikkirama
Pandisvaramudaiya nayanar temple - Later Pandya - 13th century A.D., - Records that this
particular stone pillar was the gift of a certain Thenanavan Dhanapalan a bhattan of
Konangur and this gift seems to have been made by him to thank God for having blessed
him with a son by name Udampirappalakiyan, accepting his prayers.
9. On the stone pillar mandapa seen in front of the Nataraja mandapa in
Vikkramapandisvaramudaiyar temple - Later Pandya - 13th century A.D., - Records that
this stone pillar was the gift of certain Aman Devan Thenmoliyakan Dhanapalan.
10. Inscription noticed in the stone pillar mandapam seen in front of the Nataraja
mandapam in Vikkiramapandisvaramudaiyar temple - Later Pandya - 13th century A.D., -
Records the name of a certain Palli suryan alias Soman Devan.
191
